title: Typed response contracts + fallback orchestration - demo with LumenEdge
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked LumenEdge through typed response contracts (JSON mode) for deterministic outputs, function/tool calling with fallback orchestration, and Console/Optimize controls for cost/latency tradeoffs. Security questions (KMS, audit logs, VPC) were raised; next steps: pilot scope, security pack, and benchmark run.
topics: Optimize: batching, KV caching, quant profiles
Security: KMS, audit logs, SOC2, private deploy options
action_items: Maya - send pilot pricing and the dedicated pricing sheet by 2025-11-20
Rafael - share example contract test harness and example schema + validator link (GH gist) by 2025-11-19
Priya - schedule a 2-hour bench run with LumenEdge's infra team (proposed 2025-11-25)
Sofia - to provide list of required compliance artifacts (SOC2 scope, retention) by 2025-11-21
next_steps: Redwood to deliver security pack (SOC2 summary, KMS integration doc, audit log sample)
Set up pilot environment: 2-week POC on Dedicated with a small model variant and traffic mirroring
Run contract validation tests against 3 prompt families, capture regression metrics in Console
Follow-up technical deep dive (SE-led) scheduled after Sofia's artifact list is received
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-18
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~62 minutes
Recording: Fireflies auto
Links: Deck: https://redwood.com/decks/typed-contracts (shared), GH gist: example-contracts (Rafael)

00:00 - Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, uh, from Redwood, I'm Maya, AE on this account. Rafael is our SE, Priya's gonna help on the bench. Could you do quick intros?
00:14 - Alex Murphy: Yeah hi, Alex here, CTO at LumenEdge, running our inference platform, mainly Rust+TF serving, looking at moving some features to managed inference.
00:26 - Dana Park: Dana, PM, focusing on our insights assistant, we need reliable JSON outputs for downstream analytics.
00:35 - Sofia Rivera: Sofia, security lead. SOC2 scope, KMS, and audit logs are big asks.
00:42 - Omar Hassan: Omar, ML Eng, responsible for model validation and CI.
00:48 - Maya Chen: Great. Rafael, kick us off on the typed response piece.
01:00 - Rafael Ortiz: Sure. So the core is JSON mode — we let you provide a strict schema (JSON Schema or a simplified contract) and the model is guided to produce parsed output. There's a validator step in the runtime and in the Console you can see parse success rates. It's not just soft prompting; we check shape and types server-side and can reject or auto-correct via transforms.
01:28 - Dana Park: So you'll enforce types even on streaming? We need streaming for UX.
01:36 - Rafael Ortiz: Good question. For streaming we emit a streaming envelope: partial chunks annotated with validation states. If a chunk violates schema we can either buffer until corrected or fallback to a compact text fallback. It's configurable per route.
01:58 - Omar Hassan: And how do you handle tool calling? We have a ticketing system and an internal DB query tool we'd like the model to call.
02:08 - Priya Singh: Function calling is modeled as a first-class capability — you register tools (with input/output schema). The runtime enforces that tool inputs are validated. We also support ephemeral function tokens, and RBAC for who can register/execute tools.
02:28 - Sofia Rivera: RBAC and audit logs are must-haves. If a tool emits PII, we need it to be auditable and optionally scrubbed.
02:36 - Rafael Ortiz: Yep, audit trails are logged per-token; Console shows who invoked what tool, the input payload hash, and you can configure payload redaction. We also integrate with customer KMS for envelope encryption.
03:02 - Alex Murphy: Can you demonstrate a sample flow where the model tries to call a tool but fails and Redwood handles a fallback?
03:08 - Rafael Ortiz: Absolutely. I'll share my screen - demo flow: typed response contract for a support triage action, tool = createTicket(ticketSchema), fallback = generateDraftEmail(textBlob).
03:33 - [screen share noise, some background typing]
04:05 - Rafael Ortiz: Okay sending prompt now... (simulated load) The model returned a malformed ticket id, the validator rejected it. Because this route has an explicit fallback orchestration policy, the runtime invoked the fallback: we generated a draft email object that conforms to the schema and returned that to client with a warning field. You can see the event in Console under 'Route events' with status: validated->fallback.
04:40 - Dana Park: That warning field - is it user-visible? We want analytics to see fallback rate but not necessarily surface to end-user.
04:48 - Rafael Ortiz: You can map warning fields to internal telemetry only. We have a flag: expose_warnings_to_client: false/true at route-level.
05:02 - Omar Hassan: How about retries? If createTicket fails transiently, do you retry at runtime or push that to client?
05:12 - Priya Singh: There's a retry policy editor in Console. You can set backoff, max attempts, and conditional retry on error codes. For idempotent tools we recommend retries; for non-idempotent (createTicket) use a dedupe token or server-side idempotency key.
05:35 - Sofia Rivera: What about compliance — KMS integration and private deploy?
05:40 - Rafael Ortiz: We offer KMS/HSM integration for both hosted and Dedicated; Private deployment supports customer-managed key stores and air-gapped installs. Audit logs are exportable to your SIEM.
06:01 - Alex Murphy: Latency concerns — if we add validation and fallbacks does p99 blow up?
06:08 - Rafael Ortiz: Validation is optimized; typical overhead is 5-20ms for schema checks. Fallbacks add an extra hop only when triggered. In Optimize we can suggest batching and KV prefix caching to reduce token count.
06:26 - Maya Chen: I'm going to show the Console now — Rafael, you can narrate.
06:33 - [Console UI: Route config open]
06:40 - Rafael Ortiz: Here is the route config: JSON mode enabled, contract attached (we support JSON Schema Draft7 and simplified typed contracts). You can toggle enforcement: "enforce_strict", "auto_fix" and "fallback_route".
07:02 - [UI flicker]
07:10 - Rafael Ortiz: Notice the 'Contract tests' section — we run prompt vectors and surface which tests are failing. You can add synthetic tests and see a regression graph over time.
07:28 - Dana Park: Can we version contracts? Our prompts change weekly.
07:33 - Rafael Ortiz: Yes — contract versioning and rollbacks are first-class. You can do canary rollouts of new contracts to a subset of traffic and rollback automatically if regressions exceed thresholds.
07:52 - Omar Hassan: Show us Optimize suggestions.
07:55 - Priya Singh: Optimize analyzes token distributions and suggests config: batching window, KV cache TTLs, and a quantization profile tailored to your model family and sequence length. For example, for your short-turn assistant, it recommended q4_0 type with a specific kernel path to get 2x cost reduction with <2% quality delta.
08:20 - Alex Murphy: Any examples of guardrails for hallucination?
08:25 - Rafael Ortiz: We support grounding heuristics: citation extraction + source checks. In JSON mode you can include a 'sources' array in the contract; the runtime will attach source provenances and you can configure a hard fail if no sources are present.
08:46 - Dana Park: Does that break streaming?
08:49 - Rafael Ortiz: It requires a small buffer for provenance collection; tradeoff is a bit more latency but stronger determinism.
09:05 - [15 min jump — midcall discussion about pilot scope and infra]
24:12 - Alex Murphy: For pilot we'd like dedicated small cluster in us-west, model pin to an open Llama variant, and traffic mirroring from prod. Cost predictability is important.
24:26 - Maya Chen: That's feasible — Dedicated reserved capacity can give predictable throughput and isolates your workload. We'll propose a 2-week pilot with a cap and telemetry.
24:40 - Sofia Rivera: Also need encryption-in-transit and at-rest guarantees, and audit exports to Splunk.
24:50 - Rafael Ortiz: We'll include steps for KMS MNA, and the audit export format is JSONL. We'll include sample payloads.
25:05 - Omar Hassan: On the integration side, do you have SDKs that support function registration and type-safe invocation?
25:13 - Priya Singh: Yes — SDKs for Node, Python, and Go. They include a typegen tool that can generate client stubs from the contract to ensure compile-time safety.
25:30 - Dana Park: Edge case: sometimes the model writes strings where we want ints. Will the validator coerce?
25:38 - Rafael Ortiz: There is an option 'coerce_types' that can attempt safe coercions; otherwise it flags for fallback. We recommend strict enforcement for analytics pipelines.
25:50 - Maya Chen: Quick demo of a failure-to-fallback audit in Console — Rafael?
26:00 - Rafael Ortiz: Pulling 'Route events' now — here's an event stream: request ID, contract validation status, fallback invoked, tools called, response size, and p50/p95 latency. You can click into the event to see the parsed payload and the original text transcript.
26:30 - Dana Park: How do we surface this to our SREs?
26:34 - Priya Singh: Webhooks and SIEM exports; plus a Grafana plugin if you want dashboards inside your cluster.
26:45 - [Questions from Sofia on data retention policy]
27:05 - Sofia Rivera: What's retention default?
27:09 - Rafael Ortiz: Hosted default is 30 days; Dedicated and Private can set custom retention, down to zero retention if required by policy.
27:22 - Sofia Rivera: Any PII scrubbing built-in?
27:25 - Priya Singh: Yes auto-redaction rules plus regex-based processors and a training-mode detector you can enable to catch custom tokens.
27:40 - Alex Murphy: Ok, pricing ballpark for a pilot?
27:46 - Maya Chen: We'll send a pilot quote with Dedicated reserved pricing and an add-on for extended telemetry.
28:02 - [Later in call — specific technical deep dive requests]
45:12 - Omar Hassan: We want deterministic test harness — can you run the same prompt sets and persist KW cache snapshots?
45:22 - Rafael Ortiz: We allow recording of KV cache artifacts for reproducibility and replay tests. Also Console supports a 'contract validator runner' for nightly CI.
45:40 - Dana Park: If we detect regressions, can the system auto-fallback to an older contract?
45:46 - Rafael Ortiz: Yes; rollback policies can be automatic when regression thresholds are met.
46:00 - Maya Chen: Recap — we'll send security pack, pilot pricing, Rafael will share contract examples and a test harness gist, Priya to schedule bench run. Sofia will provide compliance artifact list.
46:18 - Alex Murphy: Sounds good. Any blockers from Redwood?
46:22 - Maya Chen: None; just waiting on Sofia's artifact list and your confirmation of pilot dates.
46:30 - [wrap up pleasantries]
61:50 - Call ends.

Notes about transcription errors: Fireflies mislabels some speakers in the event stream and mis-heard acronyms (e.g., KV cache sometimes transcribed as "K-V cash"). There are minor punctuation errors above.
